record.context_brief: Graphs containing all cycle lengths up to n
record.original_question: Let g(n) denote the least number of edges of a graph that contains a cycle of length k for every integer k with 1 ≤ k ≤ n. Is g(n) = n + log₂ n + O(1) as n → ∞?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.16 (Jia[25]) g(n) = n + log2 n + O(1), as n → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer $n \geq 3$, let $g(n)$ denote the minimum number of edges of a (simple, finite, undirected) graph $G$ such that, for every integer $k$ with $3 \leq k \leq n$, the graph $G$ contains a cycle of length $k$. Determine whether
$$g(n) = n + \log_2 n + O(1) \quad \text{as } n \to \infty,$$
i.e., whether there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that $|g(n) - n - \log_2 n| \leq C$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

(Known bounds include $n + \log_2 n - 1 \leq g(n) \leq n + \log_2 n + O(\log_2 \log_2 n)$ for sufficiently large $n$.)
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is attributed to Jia and remains open. Surveys on open problems on cycles state $n + \log_2 n - 1 \leq g(n) \leq n + \log_2 n + O(\log_2 \log_2 n)$ for sufficiently large $n$, and explicitly remark that the tighter bound $g(n) = n + \log_2 n + O(1)$ "seems difficult to prove."

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on cycles (Lai, Liu)
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture (Jia): g(n) = n + log2 n + O(1), as n → ∞. Known: n + log2 n − 1 ≤ g(n) ≤ n + log2 n + O(log2 log2 n).
status_evidence.claim: The Jia conjecture is stated as open, with only weaker upper bounds known.

status_evidence.title: Extremal problems for cycles in graphs (Verstraëte survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of extremal cycle-length problems including minimum edge counts for graphs containing all short cycle lengths.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is discussed in the survey context as part of the unresolved extremal landscape.
